verdict.rationale: Hatchet's own docs say it can expose its workflows and tasks as tools that the Claude Agent SDK and OpenAI Agents SDK can invoke, and it publishes cookbooks for both SDKs. That is a real, documented link between agent frameworks and durable Hatchet execution. However, the evidence shows these as cookbook patterns and tool exposure, not wrappers that make agent steps durable automatically without glue code. missing for 10: first-party wrappers for AI SDKs and model providers that make agent steps durable automatically, coverage beyond the Claude and OpenAI Agents SDKs, detail on how much glue code remains, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an agent builder, first-party integrations wrap my AI stack — AI SDKs, agent frameworks, model providers — so agent steps get durability without glue code

citations.quote: expose Hatchet workflows and standalone tasks as tools that frameworks like the Claude Agent SDK and OpenAI Agents SDK can invoke
